bull.b: Sustained retention above 140% and strong TPV retention indicate merchants are increasing their use of dLocal. This supports durable share-of-wallet gains, deeper platform integration and recurring volume growth across emerging-market payment flows.

Rapid TPV growth, raised full-year guidance and improving operating leverage show that platform investments and merchant expansion are translating into scale. Higher volumes can support sustained profit growth as technology and operating costs grow more slowly.

Minimal leverage reduces financial risk and preserves flexibility to invest in product development, licenses and market expansion. Strong returns on equity also indicate that dLocal is generating substantial profitability from its existing capital base.

bear.b: Margin compression and lower take rates can limit the profitability of future TPV growth. Greater local-to-local, payout and large-merchant volumes may carry lower pricing, requiring continued cost control to preserve operating leverage.

The recent cash-flow rebound is strong, but the prior negative year demonstrates exposure to working-capital timing and payment-flow volatility. Inconsistent conversion could reduce the funds available for reinvestment, buybacks and strategic expansion.

dLocal's emerging-market footprint creates lasting exposure to currency movements, changing payment mixes, regional processing costs and tax rules. These factors can produce uneven margins and reduce the predictability of earnings despite strong underlying volume growth.
